review_scope: Evidence-grounded algorithm review only. No new numerical result, frozen claim, formal figure contract, paper file, state file, or release artifact was created.

current_method.decomposition: six regions are solved separately; each region is partitioned into contiguous blocks
current_method.block_policy: 14 blocks of 168 h plus one final 55 h block per region
current_method.state_coupling: terminal SOC of a block is carried to the next block as a lower-bound target
objective_components: normalized operating cost including grid purchase and export revenue
current_method.fallback: valley-charge/peak-discharge rule only after two consecutive MILP failures or time limits

strengths: Binary charge/discharge modes are enforced in the claim-eligible rolling and stress solves.
Contiguous block bookkeeping gives exact 0-2406 h coverage and a reproducible operating policy.
Candidate and baseline share metric definitions, row keys, loads, and hard-constraint audits.
Empirical 72 h stress probes are useful deterministic risk probes without requiring a probability model.
limitations: Separate regional solves do not optimize inter-region power flow or task migration jointly.
A 168 h partition can miss arbitrage across boundaries; SOC lower-bound carry can leave inventory at the end of a block and does not establish a terminal equality.
The current compatibility summary does not establish a global 2407 h binary-MILP optimum.
The relaxed full-horizon LP is permanently unusable as evidence because RegionF has simultaneous charge/discharge.
The complete audit ledger is 269/270, so an all-audits-passed sentence is prohibited.
The maximum facility-load residual is rounding-scale but exceeds the generic 5e-5 MW tolerance by about 4.50e-7 MW; exact equality must not be claimed.

innovation_candidates_ranked.method: adaptive rolling horizon with overlap and terminal inventory target
innovation_candidates_ranked.reason: Directly addresses the only structural approximation in the full-horizon policy while preserving binary MILP auditability and the existing baseline.
innovation_candidates_ranked.scope: same supplied 0-2406 h rows; no forecast or synthetic data
innovation_candidates_ranked.not_claimed_until: all coverage, mutex, SOC, load-balance, grid-cap, and comparable-baseline audits pass

innovation_candidates_ranked.method: empirical budgeted robust MILP over the four declared 72 h stress factors
innovation_candidates_ranked.reason: Converts the current post-hoc scenario probes into a bounded worst-case objective or common peak budget without inventing scenario probabilities.
innovation_candidates_ranked.scope: only the observed-data-derived factors already frozen in Q3
innovation_candidates_ranked.not_claimed_until: scenario-wise feasibility and same-output baseline comparisons are rerun

innovation_candidates_ranked.method: Benders or column generation for a future joint region/task model
innovation_candidates_ranked.reason: A decomposition method is justified only after inter-region flow or task-storage coupling is explicitly introduced; it is unnecessary for the present separable regional model.
innovation_candidates_ranked.scope: design note only; do not run or claim now

claim_boundaries: Report a deterministic rolling policy and its same-input comparison, never a globally optimal 2407 h schedule.
Report 90 successful binary-MILP blocks and exact coverage 0-2406 h; do not collapse them into one global solve.
Report 269/270 complete audits and identify the excluded LP probe; do not write 270/270.
Describe the four stress probes as deterministic observed-data-derived tests, not stochastic guarantees or forecast probabilities.
Describe the facility-load residual numerically as rounding-scale; do not call it exact equality.
Do not report fallback effectiveness because zero blocks activated it.
Negative cost values are net export revenue under the declared metric and are not negative energy demand.

risk_register.risk: Boundary SOC artifacts and horizon myopia
risk_register.evidence: Each rolling block receives a lower-bound terminal target; equality to the incoming SOC is not imposed.
risk_register.probe: Compare current lower-bound carry with terminal equality and a terminal-inventory penalty on the same 72 h and 168 h windows.
risk_register.failure_signal: terminal SOC exceeds 0.8 of capacity in more than half of audited windows, or any aggregate cost/carbon/peak metric changes by more than 5 percent.
risk_register.mitigation: Use adaptive horizon and an explicit terminal target; retain the current route only if sensitivity is small and all audits pass.

risk_register.risk: Fixed 168 h alignment hides diurnal or price-boundary effects
risk_register.evidence: The full result is assembled from fixed contiguous blocks with a 55 h tail.
risk_register.probe: Re-run the same data with a 24 h offset and a data-driven 72/168 h choice; audit duplicate and missing hours.
risk_register.failure_signal: relative metric spread over 5 percent, or any hour is missing/duplicated.
risk_register.mitigation: Use overlap and choose the shortest window that keeps all audits valid and runtime bounded.

risk_register.risk: The regional Q3 formulation does not expose a binary grid-import/export mutex in its current summary
risk_register.evidence: The frozen audit reports the result, but the claim-eligible formulation boundary is weaker than Q4's explicit grid mutex.
risk_register.probe: Add one binary grid-mode variable per hour with import/export big-M bounds and re-run the four declared stress windows plus aggregate representatives.
risk_register.failure_signal: simultaneous grid purchase and sell exceeds 5e-5 MW, or the new audit fails.
risk_register.mitigation: Make the mutex structural; if outputs are unchanged, keep the deterministic policy and record the no-change result.

risk_register.risk: A manuscript or figure turns rounded facility load into an exact identity
risk_register.evidence: Maximum residual is 5.044995509706496e-5 MW and the generic tolerance is exceeded by about 4.50e-7 MW.
risk_register.probe: Show the residual distribution and recompute from stored load components before every freeze.
risk_register.failure_signal: A claim, axis annotation, or caption says exact equality.
risk_register.mitigation: Use measured residual wording and units in all prose and figures.

risk_register.risk: A relaxed LP is mistakenly used as a scalability or quality baseline
risk_register.evidence: RegionF simultaneous charge/discharge is 116.60975349482445 MW in the full-cycle LP probe.
risk_register.probe: No further use of that probe; only binary-MILP or audited policy outputs may enter claims.
risk_register.failure_signal: Any metric, row, or chart source points to the excluded LP.
risk_register.mitigation: Quarantine the probe permanently and repeat the exclusion check at G5.

minimal_increment_experiments.purpose: Measure whether boundary SOC and fixed-window choices materially alter the reported policy.
minimal_increment_experiments.inputs: Reuse the exact supplied rows and the existing four deterministic stress factors; no new data.
variants: current: 168 h blocks, SOC_T >= SOC_0 at each block
terminal-equality: SOC_T = SOC_0 on 72 h and 168 h probes
offset/adaptive: 24 h block-start offset and H=72 when local 24 h load/renewable variability is above the empirical P75, otherwise H=168
measurements: cost, carbon, positive net-import peak, renewable utilization, curtailment, runtime
coverage, duplicate/missing hours, all SOC and power residuals
acceptance: candidate and no-storage baseline have identical row keys and metric definitions
all binary modes and all hard audits pass
no new claim is frozen from a variant until its hash and run manifest are reviewed
minimal_increment_experiments.activation_trigger: Activate terminal-equality or adaptive-window route if the boundary diagnostic or any aggregate metric changes by more than 5 percent; otherwise retain 168 h with an explicit sensitivity note.
failure_modes: window selection creates gaps or duplicate hours
terminal equality makes a block infeasible
adaptive route increases runtime by more than 2x without multi-metric gain
minimal_increment_experiments.claim_rule: A successful sensitivity run supports only a deterministic robustness statement; it does not upgrade the result to full-horizon global optimality.

minimal_increment_experiments.purpose: Close the structural gap between the Q3 formulation and the explicit Q4 grid import/export mutex.
minimal_increment_experiments.inputs: Same Q3 candidate and no-storage baseline on the four declared 72 h probes and one representative 168 h rolling block per region.
minimal_increment_experiments.model_change: Add binary g_t and bounds GridLoad_t + GridCharge_t <= ImportCap*g_t; Sell_t <= ExportCap*(1-g_t). Keep charge/discharge mutex unchanged.
measurements: cost, carbon, peak, curtailment, renewable utilization
minimal_increment_experiments.activation_trigger: Mandatory if simultaneous buy/sell is above 5e-5 MW or any audit fails; otherwise compare metrics and retain the simpler route only when the audited outputs agree within declared tolerance.
failure_modes: big-M too loose and numerical instability
new binary mode causes time-limit or infeasible blocks
baseline is changed asymmetrically
minimal_increment_experiments.claim_rule: Do not claim an improvement from the mutex patch unless the same-input baseline is rerun and all output classes remain comparable.

minimal_increment_experiments.purpose: Test a bounded robust counterpart instead of only scenario-wise reoptimization.
minimal_increment_experiments.inputs: Only the four already declared empirical factors: peak price 1.20, high carbon 1.20, renewable low 0.85, and their joint stress.
minimal_increment_experiments.design: Use a worst-case epigraph z >= normalized objective for each scenario, with a budget Gamma in {0,1,2}; preserve binary modes and SOC feasibility for every scenario.
minimal_increment_experiments.activation_trigger: Run only if the existing stress metrics show more than 10 percent spread in at least one primary metric or if the window-sensitivity route is materially unstable.
minimal_increment_experiments.acceptance: All scenario candidate/baseline audits pass; Gamma=0 reproduces the current deterministic reference within tolerance; no probability-weighted statement is made.
failure_modes: robust objective becomes dominated by one extreme factor
infeasibility caused by over-conservative renewable lower bound
scenario variables are incorrectly allowed to anticipate future information
minimal_increment_experiments.claim_rule: At most a bounded observed-data-derived worst-case comparison, never a stochastic guarantee.

fallback_policy.current_trigger: two consecutive MILP failures or time limits in the same rolling subproblem
fallback_policy.recommendation: Keep one fallback only; do not introduce a second heuristic while the primary binary route remains feasible.
fallback_policy.claim_boundary: No fallback performance or superiority claim is eligible because it was never activated.

current_method.class: integrated six-region binary storage MILP with a system peak epigraph
current_method.coupling: six storage systems are solved jointly over a fixed 72 h load envelope generated from a fixed Q2 schedule
current_method.scenario_policy: five deterministic observed-data-derived scenarios, solved as bounded scenario-wise reoptimizations
current_method.peak_selection: 17-point discrete peak-weight scan on a separate 24 h low-renewable probe; selected weight is the first audited point meeting the data-derived midpoint peak target
current_method.baseline: fixed FIFO Q2 schedule plus renewable-first no-storage balance

strengths: The integrated six-region MILP directly enforces both binary mutex pairs and SOC/energy/peak linkage.
All five bounded scenarios and all 17 discrete peak-scan points passed the declared hard audits.
The same Q2-derived window and output metrics make the candidate/baseline comparison reproducible.
limitations: Q4 fixes Q2 task schedules, so the comparison is a sequential bundle and cannot isolate scheduling from storage effects.
The 72 h result and 24 h peak probe are not full-horizon results and do not support global task-storage optimality.
Scenario-wise reoptimization is not a nonanticipative policy and has no probability-weighted interpretation.
The selected peak weight and discrete marginal are scan descriptors, not an LP dual or continuous shadow price.
A negative signed net-import peak indicates net export; it must not be conflated with a positive demand peak.

innovation_candidates_ranked.method: four-cell scheduling-storage attribution with a difference-in-differences interaction term
innovation_candidates_ranked.reason: Separates the Q2 scheduling contribution from the Q4 storage contribution using the same 72 h envelope and same metric definitions.
innovation_candidates_ranked.not_claimed_until: all four cells have identical task identities, envelope rules, and hard audits

innovation_candidates_ranked.method: epsilon-constraint Pareto scan for peak versus cost/carbon
innovation_candidates_ranked.reason: Replaces interpretation of an arbitrary weighted-sum coefficient with explicit audited peak budgets while preserving the MILP core.
innovation_candidates_ranked.not_claimed_until: each budget point is independently solved and audited

innovation_candidates_ranked.method: two-stage empirical scenario-robust MILP with shared binary mode and continuous recourse
innovation_candidates_ranked.reason: Tests whether one nonanticipative storage mode remains feasible across the five observed-data-derived scenarios.
innovation_candidates_ranked.not_claimed_until: scenario nonanticipativity, SOC transition, grid mutex, and baseline comparability are all audited

innovation_candidates_ranked.method: Benders decomposition for a future task-storage joint model
innovation_candidates_ranked.reason: Useful only when task assignment and storage dispatch are placed in one model; it is not needed for the current fixed-envelope MILP.
innovation_candidates_ranked.scope: design option, no run or claim now

claim_boundaries: State the Q4 result as an audited sequential comparison on the fixed 72 h Q2-derived window.
Keep the five scenarios deterministic observed-data-derived probes; no probability or chance constraint is implied.
Treat the selected 0.0003 weight and 2.35298451326919e-8/MW value as discrete scan descriptors only.
Treat 94.51503392666643 MW as the independent 24 h low-renewable peak-probe reduction, not a full-horizon reduction.
Do not attribute the low-renewable cost/carbon differences to storage alone until the four-cell attribution experiment is run.
Do not claim joint task-storage or full-horizon global optimality.

risk_register.risk: Q2 scheduling and Q4 storage effects are bundled
risk_register.evidence: Candidate is Q2 schedule plus storage while baseline is FIFO schedule plus no storage.
risk_register.probe: Run four cells: FIFO/no-storage, candidate/no-storage, FIFO/storage, candidate/storage on the same 72 h window and five scenarios.
risk_register.failure_signal: The interaction term changes sign across scenarios or one cell fails a hard audit.
risk_register.mitigation: Report descriptive decomposition only; avoid causal wording.

risk_register.risk: A weighted-sum scan is read as a continuous marginal price
risk_register.evidence: Peak response is evaluated at 17 discrete weights and the frozen value is explicitly discrete.
risk_register.probe: Use audited epsilon-constraint peak budgets around the first active scan point.
risk_register.failure_signal: Peak changes in a large step or the selected point is unstable under a neighboring budget.
risk_register.mitigation: Plot ordered discrete points and label the quantity as a scan descriptor.

risk_register.risk: Scenario-wise reoptimization uses future scenario information
risk_register.evidence: Each scenario is solved separately on the same bounded window.
risk_register.probe: Share binary mode variables across scenarios and allow only continuous recourse, or impose a common peak budget with scenario-specific dispatch.
risk_register.failure_signal: Shared-mode model becomes infeasible or loses all improvements under the declared scenarios.
risk_register.mitigation: Retain scenario-wise runs as stress diagnostics, not an implementable robust policy.

risk_register.risk: 72 h and 24 h windows do not reveal full-horizon SOC drift
risk_register.evidence: Summary explicitly states that no full-horizon result is claimed.
risk_register.probe: Chain contiguous 72 h windows with SOC carry and compare to the single-window reference on overlapping boundaries.
risk_register.failure_signal: SOC boundary mismatch, infeasible continuation, or >5 percent metric drift.
risk_register.mitigation: Use a rolling Q4 policy or keep the bounded-window scope explicit.

risk_register.risk: Net export is displayed as a negative demand peak
risk_register.evidence: The low-renewable candidate signed maximum is -167.07850046 MW, while the positive-part peak is the demand measure.
risk_register.probe: Audit signed peak and positive-part peak as separate fields for every scenario.
risk_register.failure_signal: A chart or caption uses negative signed peak as a positive load reduction without definition.
risk_register.mitigation: Use positive-part peak for demand figures and a separate signed export annotation.

minimal_increment_experiments.purpose: Separate scheduling, storage, and their interaction before interpreting Q4 gains.
cells: A = FIFO schedule + no storage (existing baseline)
B = Q2 candidate schedule + no storage
C = FIFO schedule + integrated storage MILP
D = Q2 candidate schedule + integrated storage MILP (existing candidate)
minimal_increment_experiments.scope: same 72 h window, same five scenarios, same task identities, PUE/load reconstruction, and metric definitions
derived_effects: storage effect under candidate scheduling = D - B
storage effect under FIFO scheduling = C - A
scheduling effect with storage = D - C
interaction = (D - B) - (C - A), reported separately for cost, carbon, and positive peak
acceptance: all four cells pass task identity, energy balance, SOC, mutex, grid-cap, and peak-linkage audits
B and D use the same candidate task envelope; A and C use the same FIFO envelope
no effect is described as causal; it is a conditional decomposition under fixed data
minimal_increment_experiments.activation_trigger: Run immediately before any Q4 paragraph that attributes a gain specifically to storage or specifically to Q2 scheduling.
failure_modes: task spill or closeout handling differs between cells
baseline is given a different renewable or terminal-SOC convention
one cell uses a different peak definition
minimal_increment_experiments.claim_rule: Only the frozen aggregate bundle claim remains eligible until this experiment is hashed and reviewed.

minimal_increment_experiments.purpose: Make peak selection auditable as an explicit budget rather than a continuous price interpretation.
minimal_increment_experiments.design: On the existing 24 h low-renewable probe, solve min(normalized cost + carbon + curtailment) subject to positive system peak <= {291.6033, 0.75*291.6033, 0.5*291.6033, 197.0883} MW; retain binary mutex and terminal SOC equality.
minimal_increment_experiments.comparison: Compare the epsilon frontier with the 17-point weighted scan, including the selected 0.0003 point.
minimal_increment_experiments.activation_trigger: Activated by the observed 94.51503392666643 MW step from zero-weight to selected scan point; use the scan only as a reference, not a shadow-price estimate.
minimal_increment_experiments.acceptance: Every budget point solves and passes hard audits; infeasible budgets are recorded rather than silently discarded.
failure_modes: peak bound is below physical feasibility
objective scaling changes the ranking of cost and carbon
positive-part and signed peak are mixed
minimal_increment_experiments.claim_rule: Report an audited discrete Pareto/budget frontier; do not call any finite-difference value a dual price.

minimal_increment_experiments.purpose: Check whether the 72 h endpoint and terminal SOC equality remain stable when the policy is chained.
minimal_increment_experiments.design: Use contiguous existing rows in four 72 h windows around the Q2 horizon; carry SOC forward, enforce equality only at the declared end-of-cycle target, and compare the central window with the frozen 72 h result.
minimal_increment_experiments.activation_trigger: Run if Q4-E1 shows a material storage contribution or if adjacent-window peak/renewable regimes differ materially by a predeclared 10 percent diagnostic.
failure_modes: window endpoints omit closeout tasks
terminal equality creates artificial charging
scenario factors are applied outside their declared scope
minimal_increment_experiments.claim_rule: A pass supports chained bounded-window robustness only; it does not establish a global optimum.

minimal_increment_experiments.purpose: Test a nonanticipative robust storage policy over the five declared scenarios.
minimal_increment_experiments.design: Share charge/discharge and grid import/export binary modes across scenarios; retain scenario-specific continuous power/SOC recourse and a common positive-peak epigraph.
minimal_increment_experiments.activation_trigger: Activate when scenario-wise positive peak or cost spread exceeds 10 percent, or when Q4-E3 reports material boundary drift.
minimal_increment_experiments.acceptance: All five scenario dispatches and the same-input baseline pass hard audits; observed-scenario output remains within the current reference tolerance.
failure_modes: shared binaries make the model infeasible
recourse violates SOC carry or grid caps
scenario transformations are incorrectly interpreted probabilistically
minimal_increment_experiments.claim_rule: If successful, claim only a deterministic observed-factor robust policy; otherwise retain current scenario-wise diagnostics.

fallback_policy.recommendation: Do not add a heuristic fallback until a time-limit or infeasibility trigger is observed; if needed, allow one explicitly named feasibility-only rule and audit it against the same baseline.
fallback_policy.claim_boundary: No fallback effectiveness statement is permitted without an activated run and frozen evidence.

cross_question_integration.current_data_flow: Q1 forecast and reconciliation -> Q2 fixed deterministic task schedule -> Q3 regional rolling storage policy and empirical stress factors -> Q4 fixed-envelope integrated storage and peak probe
main_interface_risks: Q2 task assignment is treated as fixed input in Q4, so Q4 cannot be read as a joint scheduler-storage optimizer.
Q3 terminal SOC convention differs from Q4 terminal equality; any combined narrative must state the distinction.
Q3 uses regional decomposition while Q4 uses six-region integration; the scope change is methodological, not evidence of a network-flow model.
recommended_sequence: First run Q3-E1 and Q3-E2 plus Q4-E1 and Q4-E2 as P0 structural checks.
If boundary or scenario spread is material, run the corresponding adaptive or robust conditional experiment; otherwise keep the audited compatibility routes.
Only after the selected routes pass should new figures be promoted from staging and claims be reconsidered by the root agent.
Use Benders/column generation only if an explicit task-storage or inter-region coupling model is actually introduced.
cross_question_integration.model_selection_rule: Prefer the simplest audited binary MILP or deterministic rolling policy that preserves common-input baseline comparability; upgrade only when a predeclared trigger and real-data gain justify the added complexity.
